寝.meaning: Under the <part>roof</part>, a farmer leans his <part>climbing pole</part> and his <part>rake</part> against the wall, pulls a <part>blanket</part> over his head and twists into a <part>pretzel</part> on the floor, boots still on. He's done for the day. Time to <kanji>lie down</kanji>.
寝.on: He kicks off one boot in his sleep, and it bangs him on the <sound>shin</sound>.
寝.kun: Snoring, he tugs the blanket up to his <sound>ne</sound>ck.

試.meaning: Before the big <part>ceremony</part>, the mayor practises his <part>speech</part> to an empty hall. Mic on: one, two, one, two. Does it echo? Does anyone laugh at the jokes? It's only a <kanji>test</kanji>.
試.on: A knight in the back row holds up a <sound>shi</sound>eld with a score painted on it: four out of ten.
試.kun: The trial audience is a <sound>ko</sound>ala, a <sound>co</sound>conut and a <sound>ro</sound>dent, and only the coconut doesn't laugh.

服.meaning: Under the <part>moon</part>, a tailor sews all night. He twists each sleeve into a <part>pretzel</part> fold, and when the cloth won't lie flat, he presses it down with the heavy handle of a rubber <part>stamp</part>, like a tiny iron. By morning the shop is full of <kanji>clothing</kanji>.
服.on: Every shirt goes up on a big <sound>hook</sound> by the door, ready to be sold.

甘.meaning: Two posts poke up through a long bar, with a short bar held between them like a sugar cube on a tongue. The cube melts, the tongue curls, and your whole face smiles. It tastes <kanji>sweet</kanji>.
甘.on: A bee buzzes out of a pink <sound>carn</sound>ation, carrying a drop of honey.
甘.kun: You lick the honey: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' Then you run to your <sound>Ma</sound> to ask for more.

案.meaning: You <part>relax</part> in a hammock tied to a <part>tree</part>, eyes half shut. Then an idea drops on you like an acorn: a treehouse! Ladders, ropes, a slide. Before you've even sat up, you have a <kanji>plan</kanji>.
案.on: Your <sound>un</sound>cle reads it, nods, and goes to fetch his saw.
案.kun: You spread the plans out, sneeze '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo and its <sound>e</sound>gg roll off the wooden top: a desk.

冬.meaning: Someone leaves a <part>folding chair</part> out on the porch, and by morning two chips of <part>ice</part> hang under its seat. The pond is frozen, the trees are bare, and nobody will sit outside for months. It's <kanji>winter</kanji>.
冬.on: You step out barefoot and stub your frozen <sound>toe</sound> on the chair.
冬.kun: Back inside, you hide under your <sound>fu</sound>ton and strum a sad song on your <sound>u</sound>kulele.

建.meaning: A painter dips a giant <part>brush</part> in wet cement and crosses an empty lot with one <part>long stride</part> after another, painting walls straight up out of the ground. By sunset there's a whole house. That's how he likes to <kanji>build</kanji>.
建.on: He starts small: first he paints a <sound>ken</sound>nel for his dog.
建.kun: Then he paints a stall for his <sound>ta</sound>co truck right next door.
